theory.intro: Use $x = \mu + z\sigma$ to convert a $z$-score to a raw score, where $\mu$ is the mean and $\sigma$ is the standard deviation.
facts: $x = \mu + z\sigma$: multiply the $z$-score by the standard deviation, then add the mean.
A positive $z$ gives a raw value above the mean; a negative $z$ gives one below the mean.
When $z$ is negative the term $z\sigma$ is negative, so you end up subtracting from the mean.
'Two standard deviations below the mean' means $z = -2$, so turn the words into a $z$-score first.
Check an answer by substituting it back into $z = \dfrac{x - \mu}{\sigma}$; it must give the original $z$-score.

workedExamples.question_text:
A test has mean $47.8$ and standard deviation $6.5$.
(a) Find the mark with $z=1.3$.
(b) Find the mark that is $1.7$ standard deviations below the mean. Give exact answers.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Use $x=\mu+z\sigma$.
(a) $x=47.8+1.3\times6.5$
$=47.8+8.45$
$=56.25$.
(b) Below the mean means $z=-1.7$.
$x=47.8+(-1.7)\times6.5$
$=47.8-11.05$
$=36.75$.
The positive score gives a mark above the mean; the negative score gives one below it.

workedExamples.question_text: The monthly rainfall at a station has a mean of $62$ mm and a standard deviation of $2.4$ mm. Find the rainfall corresponding to a standardised score of $2.7$, correct to one decimal place.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$x=\mu+z\sigma$
$=62+2.7\times2.4$
$=62+6.48$
$=68.48$ mm.
The rainfall is $68.5$ mm, correct to one decimal place.

workedExamples.question_text: A reading test has a mean mark of $68.4$ and a standard deviation of $7.6$. A student achieved a $z$-score of $-2.25$. What was the student's actual mark?

foundation.question_text:
A dataset has a mean of $\mu = 70$ and a standard deviation of $\sigma = 8$.
Find the raw value with a $z$-score of $1.5$.

A dataset has a mean of $\mu = 52$ and a standard deviation of $\sigma = 6$.
Find the raw value with a $z$-score of $-2$.

A dataset has a mean of $\mu = 48$ and a standard deviation of $\sigma = 5$.
Find the raw value with a $z$-score of $0.6$.

The marks in a test have a mean of $25$ and a standard deviation of $4$.
What mark is three standard deviations below the mean?
foundation.solution_text:
Three standard deviations below the mean means $z = -3$.
$x = \mu + z\sigma$
$= 25 + (-3) \times 4$
$= 25 - 12$
$= 13$

foundation.question_text:
The systolic blood pressure readings of a group have a mean of $140$ and a standard deviation of $15$.
What reading is $1.5$ standard deviations above the mean?
foundation.solution_text:
$1.5$ standard deviations above the mean means $z = 1.5$.
$x = \mu + z\sigma$
$= 140 + 1.5 \times 15$
$= 140 + 22.5$
$= 162.5$

foundation.question_text:
Bags of rice are filled with a mean mass of $5.02$ kg and a standard deviation of $0.04$ kg.
Find the mass of a bag with a $z$-score of $-1.25$.

development.question_text:
A dataset has a mean of $\mu = 63.5$ and a standard deviation of $\sigma = 7.2$.
Find the raw value with a $z$-score of $2.3$.

The monthly rainfall at a station has a mean of $84$ mm and a standard deviation of $12.5$ mm.
Find the rainfall of a month with a $z$-score of $-1.8$.

A test has a mean mark of $61.8$ and a standard deviation of $5.6$.
Find the mark corresponding to a $z$-score of $-1.75$.

The monthly rainfall at a station has a mean of $73$ mm and a standard deviation of $2.6$ mm.
Find the rainfall corresponding to a standardised score of $2.8$, correct to one decimal place.
development.solution_text:
$x = \mu + z\sigma$
$= 73 + 2.8 \times 2.6$
$= 73 + 7.28$
$= 80.28$ mm.
The rainfall is $80.3$ mm, correct to one decimal place.

development.question_text:
A fitness test has a mean mark of $69.5$ and a standard deviation of $7.2$.
What mark is $2.25$ standard deviations below the mean?
development.solution_text:
$2.25$ standard deviations below the mean means $z = -2.25$.
$x = \mu + z\sigma$
$= 69.5 + (-2.25) \times 7.2$
$= 69.5 - 16.2$
$= 53.3$

development.question_text:

What mark corresponds to a $z$-score of $1.75$?

mastery.question_text:
The masses of newborn lambs are normally distributed with a mean of $3.2$ kg and a standard deviation of $0.45$ kg.
Find the two masses with $z$-scores of $-2$ and $2$.

A test has a mean mark of $67.35$ and a standard deviation of $4.8$.
Find the mark corresponding to a $z$-score of $-2.125$.

A reading test has a mean mark of $58.75$ and a standard deviation of $7.6$.
What mark is $2.375$ standard deviations above the mean?
mastery.solution_text:
$2.375$ standard deviations above the mean means $z = 2.375$.
$x = \mu + z\sigma$
$= 58.75 + 2.375 \times 7.6$
$= 58.75 + 18.05$
$= 76.8$
